name: Station Observatory: inspectable session world
about: Baseline the prototype, split it into a shared model plus five parallel lenses (islands, call journeys, time, inspector, 3D), integrate, audit adversarially and hand off with a production-bridge spec.

steps.title: Baseline the Station Observatory prototype
steps.goal:
Baseline the Station Observatory prototype so every later step starts from a known state. Its files are in Git since commit bb0334e (15 November 2026), so your worktree already has them. Copy nothing from Robert's main checkout and change nothing there.

The baseline files:
- docs/ui-exploration/station.html, station.css, station.js, verify-station.py, PLAN.md, VERIFICATION.md, index.html
- docs/research/2026-11-12-session-visualization-paradigms.md
- docs/handoffs/2026-11-12-station-observatory-next-phase.md (read its section 'Updates since this brief was written' first)

1. Record git status --short and git log -3 --oneline of your worktree, your HEAD as the baseline origin, and the SHA-256 of each file above. If one is missing, or differs from HEAD (git diff --stat HEAD -- <file>), stop and report it; do not recreate a file.
2. Run node --check docs/ui-exploration/station.js, and python "<absolute worktree path>\docs\ui-exploration\verify-station.py" from a %TEMP% working directory. It needs the installed Python Playwright and Microsoft Edge; if either is unavailable, record the exact error as an environment blocker, do not claim a pass. Screenshots land in artifacts/station-prototype/ (ignored); list them.
3. Write the receipt docs/ui-exploration/observatory/receipts/baseline.md with the hash table, the exact outputs and the screenshot list.

Do not change any existing file. Commit only your receipt with the message 'chore: baseline station observatory prototype'.

Rules: Run a Plan worker; do not open cards, request plan approval or call finish self. Synthetic data only; never read real transcripts under ~/.claude or ~/.codex. After the browser check, confirm every browser or helper you started has exited and none has your worktree as its cwd; never kill processes you did not start. Never call something passed unless you ran it.
steps.reply: The commit id, the file/hash table, the baseline HEAD, exact outputs of node --check and verify-station.py, screenshot paths, and any environment blocker.

steps.title: Split the prototype into a shared model, store and lens seams
steps.goal:
Also read docs/research/2026-11-12-session-visualization-paradigms.md and docs/ui-exploration/station.html, station.css, station.js, verify-station.py. Read the header comment of docs/concepts/shared/sim.js too: its call fields (flow hops, causedBy, retryOf, error codes) served the same purpose; reuse a name where it fits, never load that file. Restructure the prototype so five parallel workers can each add one lens while editing only their own files. Do not build lens features yourself.

1. Split station.js into classic scripts under docs/ui-exploration/observatory/ on one namespace window.Observatory: model.js, store.js, layout.js, fixtures.js, feed.js, stations.js (current isometric map, controls, flat view; behaviour unchanged), inspector.js + inspector.css (current dialog; behaviour unchanged). station.html stays the entry point.
2. model.js: session {id, label, role main|subagent|unrelated, parentId, parentKnown, transcript present|missing|unreadable|loading}; call {id, sessionId, kind, tool, resourceId, requestTime, resultTime or null, status ok|error|pending|unknown, input and output each {state present|empty|omitted|unavailable, value}, correlationId, retryOf only when explicit}; edge {id, type delegation|invocation|message|shared-resource|unknown, from, to, evidence call ids}; resource {opaque id, label}. Never derive edges from timing or proximity.
3. store.js: the single source of truth: selection {sessionId, stationId, resourceId, callId, edgeId}, expanded set, focus path, mode live|paused|pinned, liveHead, viewed position, pendingCount, pins [a, b], errorsOnly, motion, speed; subscribe/dispatch. Ingestion moves the viewed position only in live mode.
4. layout.js: deterministic positions for islands, stations and child islands from the expanded set; no force simulation; new data never reflows; anchor(nodeId) for routes.
5. fixtures.js: the original 42-call demo-01 story preserved exactly (ids, times, payloads, errors) as the main session, plus: a parent with three children (one missing transcript), one unrelated session, a correlated request/result, an API failure with an explicit retry, overlapping work in two children, a shared resource, one explicit message, one unknown relation, calls with no result time, and omitted, empty and unavailable payloads. ?fixture=1|6|24 (default 6), deterministic and seeded. feed.js simulates live ingestion on a timer.
6. station.html: layers #layer-islands, #layer-routes, #layer-signals, #layer-cards, panels #panel-timeline and #panel-orbit, and tags for stub lens files islands.js/.css, journeys.js/.css, timeline.js/.css, projection.js, orbit.js/.css, each registering a no-op Observatory.lenses.<name>.
7. verify_common.py (Edge headless helper: open a fixture, collect page errors and any http(s) request, guaranteed close) and passing stubs verify-islands.py, verify-journeys.py, verify-time.py, verify-inspector.py, verify-orbit.py, plus verify-foundation.py testing store invariants (ingestion while paused keeps viewed position and selection; pendingCount increments).
8. CONTRACT.md: every API above, a file ownership table (lens -> its files), the rule that lens workers never edit shared files and log needed changes under 'Contract requests' in their receipt, and how to run each check.

Acceptance: verify-station.py passes unmodified (do not edit it); node --check passes on every script; screenshots match the baseline look; fixtures 1/6/24 load with no errors or network requests. Receipt: docs/ui-exploration/observatory/receipts/foundation.md.

Rules: no cards, plan approvals or finish self. Synthetic data only. file:// with zero network: classic scripts, no ES modules, CDN, npm packages or build. Run Playwright by absolute path from a %TEMP% cwd; afterwards confirm browsers you started exited and none has your worktree as cwd; never kill others. Subagents only opus at effort medium or haiku at effort max. Never claim a pass you did not run. Commit.
steps.reply: The commit id, the module and ownership table, the CONTRACT.md path, exact outputs of node --check, verify-station.py and verify-foundation.py, screenshot comparison, and anything left undone.

steps.title: Map real session data to the model (specification only)
steps.goal:
Write docs/ui-exploration/observatory/REAL-DATA-MAP.md, a specification only. Change no code and no tests.

Read src/transcript.js, src/sessions.js, src/detail.js, src/webview.js, src/extension.js, media/view.js, media/app.js, README.md, HANDOFF.md, the source handoff (first 'Updates since this brief was written', then 'Truth and privacy requirements' and 'Real data gaps'), docs/research/2026-11-12-session-visualization-paradigms.md and docs/research/2026-11-14-provider-sdk-architecture.md.

1. For each concept: session, parent/subagent topology, tool call, request/result correlation, durations, per-call resource association, shared resources across children, inter-session messages, payload detail, lifecycle states. Give the exact fields and functions that hold it today (file:line), what the webview receives now, what is missing, and the proposed handling: reuse, extend the normalized contract, or show as unknown.
2. Quote the current collection limits from code (FAMILY_LIMIT, MAX_EVENTS, LANE_EVENTS, SESSION_LIMIT, LIFECYCLE_LIMIT, PENDING_LIMIT, the limits in src/detail.js and any others) and how omissions are disclosed now. The handoff quotes 24 / 2,000 / 10,000; confirm or correct each. Say how the agentviz.scope setting limits which sessions are listed.
3. End times. Since details on click was added, finishTool() keeps a call's recorded end time in the host-only event.at.finished and readDetail() returns it on request, but the live event sent to the view still has five fields and no end time. Confirm this from code with file:line, say for which records no time is kept, and describe the smallest change that would send recorded end times with live events, with the regression tests it needs. Do not make the change.
4. Details on click is the product's existing local inspection contract. Describe it exactly from code: what the view asks for, what the host reads and returns, the limits, what is kept, what closing removes. Then list what the session world's inspector needs beyond it (kind-specific sections, edge ledgers, resource panels across sessions) and the decisions still open for Robert, each with a recommended default: redaction of secrets, tokens and full paths in shown text; screenshots and exported evidence; never sending content to a hosted service.
5. List provider differences (Claude vs Codex) you can confirm from code; mark anything not confirmed as unverified.
6. For each gap, say whether an official provider interface named in the 14 November research could close it (for example Codex App Server command duration and file changes). That research tested nothing: mark every such line 'untested'.

The fixture model is being defined concurrently in docs/ui-exploration/observatory/CONTRACT.md by another step. If that file is absent, use the handoff vocabulary (session, call, edge types delegation, invocation/result, message, shared resource, unknown) and list the mapping items the final step must reconcile.

Use synthetic examples only. Never read or quote real transcripts under ~/.claude or ~/.codex. Do not install an SDK, start an app server or resume a session. Receipt: docs/ui-exploration/observatory/receipts/data-bridge.md.

Rules: Run a Plan worker; do not open cards, request plan approval or call finish self. Subagents only opus at effort medium or haiku at effort max; never sonnet or fable. Commit.
steps.reply: The commit id, the REAL-DATA-MAP.md path, the confirmed limits with file:line, the decisions Robert must make, and any unverified or untested claims.

steps.title: Lens A: connected session islands and typed edges
steps.goal:
Implement lens A, Connected session islands, from section A of docs/handoffs/2026-11-12-station-observatory-next-phase.md. Edit only docs/ui-exploration/observatory/islands.js, islands.css, verify-islands.py and your receipt. Use only the store, layout and model APIs in CONTRACT.md. Four other lenses are built in parallel; never edit shared or other lens files.

Before designing, read 'Concept pages to mine, per lens' in that handoff and open the pages it names for this lens under docs/concepts/. Borrow interaction ideas only: keep the station look, and never edit or load anything in docs/concepts/.

- Each session is a stable compact island at its layout position. Expanding reveals its six tool stations and its explicitly linked children; neighbours stay visible at lower detail. Expand, collapse, focus (pan/scale to the neighbourhood), breadcrumbs for the focus path and Home all go through the store. Nothing rearranges when data arrives or another island expands, beyond layout's deterministic rule.
- Draw the five edge types distinctly by stroke, marker and a text label shown on hover and focus and in a legend: Delegation; Invocation/result; Message; Shared resource (dashed, labelled 'association, not communication'); Unknown (visibly unknown, never attached to a parent as fact). Children with parentKnown false, or a missing or unreadable transcript, say so in text.
- Every island and edge is keyboard reachable, has an accessible name, and selecting it sets store.selection; Escape returns focus. Selection survives expand and collapse.
- At 390 and 768 px provide a readable tree/list alternative to tiny map labels.
- Reduced motion: camera jumps, no animated pans.

verify-islands.py (use verify_common.py) asserts on fixture 6: parent, three children and the unrelated session present; expand, collapse, focus and Home; selection retained across collapse; every edge type rendered with its label and legend entry; the missing child shown as missing; the unknown relation not drawn as delegation; a keyboard-only path; the 390 px tree view; fixture 24 renders without page overflow; no page errors or network requests. verify-station.py must still pass unmodified.

If you need a contract change, implement a local adapter inside your files and write the request under 'Contract requests' in docs/ui-exploration/observatory/receipts/islands.md.

steps.title: Lens B: follow one call with request and result signals
steps.goal:
Implement lens B, Follow one call, from section B of docs/handoffs/2026-11-12-station-observatory-next-phase.md. Edit only docs/ui-exploration/observatory/journeys.js, journeys.css, verify-journeys.py and your receipt. Draw in #layer-routes, #layer-signals and #layer-cards using layout anchors and the store. Four other lenses are built in parallel; never edit shared or other lens files.

Before designing, read 'Concept pages to mine, per lens' in that handoff and open the pages it names for this lens under docs/concepts/. Borrow interaction ideas only: keep the station look, and never edit or load anything in docs/concepts/.

- When an event is ingested at the viewed moment, emit a request token from caller to station or service and, only when the fixture records a correlated result, a separate return token. Travel time is fixed presentation, never shown or implied as latency. A signal is an application event, not a network packet; say so in the legend.
- Every route has a stable, wide, keyboard-focusable hit target that selects its edge (store.selection.edgeId). Aggregate counts keep the exact call ids underneath. Users never have to click a moving token: each call also appears as a stationary event card in #layer-cards that stays inspectable after its animation ends.
- Selecting a call spotlights its participants and explicitly related events (same correlationId, explicit retryOf) and dims other traffic. Infer nothing else.
- Error markers persist. A later success on the same route never removes an earlier failure. Retry links are drawn only when retryOf exists.
- Show concurrent work in two children at once without ambiguity.
- Respect store.motion and prefers-reduced-motion: no tokens, but cards still appear. Pausing stops tokens while ingestion keeps counting pending events.

verify-journeys.py (use verify_common.py) asserts: every token and card carries a data-call id that exists in the fixture; return tokens only for correlated calls; a retry link only where retryOf exists; the error marker remains after a later success; a route hit target selects its edge; a keyboard route to a card; reduced motion gives zero tokens and the cards remain; no page errors or network requests. verify-station.py must still pass unmodified.

Log any needed contract change under 'Contract requests' in docs/ui-exploration/observatory/receipts/journeys.md and use a local adapter meanwhile.

steps.title: Lens C: live vs historical time, waterfall and pinned moments
steps.goal:
Implement lens C, Live and historical inspection, from section C of docs/handoffs/2026-11-12-station-observatory-next-phase.md. Edit only docs/ui-exploration/observatory/timeline.js, timeline.css, verify-time.py and your receipt; render in #panel-timeline. Before designing, read 'Concept pages to mine, per lens' in that handoff and open the pages it names for this lens under docs/concepts/. Borrow interaction ideas only: keep the station look, and never edit or load anything in docs/concepts/.

- Keep ingestion separate from viewing. In Live mode the view follows liveHead. Any inspection (selecting a call, scrubbing, pinning) switches to Paused or Pinned; the viewed moment, map, selected event and timeline then stay fixed while feed.js keeps ingesting. Show 'N new events' and a clear 'Return to live' action that restores following and clears the count. Show the last received time.
- A compact waterfall: one lane per visible session, children indented under their parent. Draw a span only where both requestTime and resultTime are recorded; a call without resultTime is a point labelled 'duration unknown'. Never compute a duration from gaps between neighbouring events. Error points stay marked.
- Pinned moments: pin A and B and compare them side by side (calls per station, errors, active sessions) with a clear difference summary, both bound to the store's pins.
- Where the fixture has both, label event time and arrival time separately.
- Clicking a span or point selects that call in the store, so the map and inspector agree.
- Keyboard: arrows move the viewed moment, Home and End jump, L returns to live; every control has an accessible name. Respect reduced motion.
- Existing play, pause, restart, speed and scrubber keep working through the store; verify-station.py must still pass unmodified.

steps.title: Lens E: optional 3D orbit view and time-slice experiment
steps.goal:
Implement the optional 3D views described in sections A and C of docs/handoffs/2026-11-12-station-observatory-next-phase.md and paradigms 1 and 8 of docs/research/2026-11-12-session-visualization-paradigms.md. Edit only docs/ui-exploration/observatory/projection.js, orbit.js, orbit.css, verify-orbit.py and your receipt; render in #panel-orbit. No library: write a small perspective projection (rotate, project, depth sort) drawing SVG or canvas, so file:// and zero network still hold. Four other lenses are built in parallel; never edit shared or other lens files.

Before designing, read 'Concept pages to mine, per lens' in that handoff and open the pages it names for this lens under docs/concepts/. Borrow interaction ideas only: keep the station look, and never edit or load anything in docs/concepts/.

- Orbit view (a toggle, off by default): the same islands, stations and edges from layout positions, lifted into shallow 3D where depth means hierarchy (children below parents). Drag to orbit, wheel to zoom, and keyboard equivalents (arrows rotate, + and - zoom, H for Home). Home restores the default readable camera. Clamp angles so labels stay readable. Selecting in 3D sets the same store selection; picking uses projected stationary hit areas, never moving tokens. Edge types keep the same styles and labels as the 2D map.
- Time-slice experiment (a separate toggle): depth means time instead, and hierarchy is flattened in this mode; the mode label says so. Stack translucent planes at time buckets, show error points and parent/child lifetime strands, a movable slice plane bound to the store's viewed position, and a flat list of the events at the slice beside it.
- Never use depth for both meanings at once. A visible label always states what depth means. A 'Back to map' action is always visible.
- Reduced motion: no inertial camera; step changes only.
- Measure frame time while orbiting on fixtures 1, 6 and 24 (requestAnimationFrame deltas over 3 s) and record median and p95 in your receipt. Do not call it smooth without numbers.

verify-orbit.py (use verify_common.py) asserts: the toggle turns the view on and off; Home restores the camera transform; a keyboard rotation changes it; a selection made in 3D reaches the store and inspector; the time-slice label says depth means time; the slice follows the viewed position; reduced motion; no page errors or network requests. verify-station.py must still pass unmodified.

Log any needed contract change under 'Contract requests' in docs/ui-exploration/observatory/receipts/orbit3d.md and use a local adapter meanwhile.

steps.title: Adversarial audit: truth, review tasks, access, privacy
steps.goal:
You are the adversarial audit of the integrated Station Observatory (docs/ui-exploration/station.html). Assume it is wrong until evidence says otherwise.

Dispatch four parallel subagents (model opus, effort medium; investigation only, no edits), one per area below. Reproduce every finding yourself before acting on it.

(a) Truth: every visible token, card, route count and edge maps to fixture call or edge ids; no edge, message or retry exists without explicit fixture evidence; a later success never removes an earlier error; durations appear only with both times; synthetic badges are present; nothing implies live data, measured latency or captured packets.
(b) Review tasks from docs/research/2026-11-12-session-visualization-paradigms.md, scripted with Playwright on fixtures 6 and 24: identify who spawned a child; find the response to one request; tell a shared-resource association from a message; explain an error's recorded preceding events; return from history to live. For each, record success, number of interactions, wrong turns and elapsed script time. State plainly that this is a scripted walk-through, not user testing.
(c) Keyboard-only completion of each task; Escape and focus return; reduced motion; 390 and 768 px.
(d) Zero http(s) requests, no payloads written to storage, no real paths or transcripts.

Write docs/ui-exploration/observatory/AUDIT.md: each finding with severity, reproduction steps and evidence. Fix every reproduced high or medium finding and add a regression assertion for it (verify-audit.py, run by verify-observatory.py). List the unfixed low findings.

Also write docs/ui-exploration/observatory/REVIEW-SCRIPT.md: a ten-minute script for Robert to try the five tasks by hand and note time taken and points of confusion.

Acceptance: verify-observatory.py passes after the fixes; AUDIT.md states what was fixed, what remains and the coverage limits. Receipt: docs/ui-exploration/observatory/receipts/audit.md.

steps.title: Deliver: demo, real vs simulated, production bridge, merge note
steps.goal:
Prepare the delivery. Write docs/ui-exploration/observatory/DELIVERY.md, short and scannable:

1. How to open the demo: station.html, the ?fixture=1, 6 and 24 URLs, and the orbit and time-slice toggles. How to run verify-observatory.py.
2. Real vs simulated: all data is synthetic; signals are application events, not packets; animation time is not latency; nothing is connected to live transcripts or the VS Code extension.
3. A table of every acceptance criterion in the source handoff: met, partly met or not met, with the evidence file and check output.
